transcript: Hey! Brain drop trip! Drop drop drop drop! This is how you create the scene building effect. The first and most important step is filming the video. Try to frame the shot with one building in the middle and two on the sides, converging towards the center. Next, add the video into your project after another clip. Free-stream the beginning of the video and set the frame as an overlay. Move it just before the original video and crop it to about 0.6 seconds. Then, duplicate it twice so you have three overlays total. On the first one, select remove background, then custom removal and highlight the left building. Repeat this with the other two overlays, selecting the right building on one and the middle on the other. Now, we'll use keyframes to create the slide-in effect. Add a keyframe at the beginning of the left building clip and move it completely out of the frame. Then, add another keyframe after about 0.2 seconds and move it back into place. Repeat this for the other two clips, starting each animation as the previous building slides in. Have the right building move in from the right and the middle slide up from the bottom. transcript: How I edited this. Welcome to Self-Stating Episode 5, Falling Through Instagram. Start by filming two clips. One of you getting up and falling, and one of you laying down and making a falling motion. It looks a little silly, but you gotta trust me. Now open CapCut or your editing software. For the intro, add the FPS lag effect to give it a stop motion look. And the black hole opening is an overlay I actually animated in Procreate, so comment woe and I'll send it to you for free. Now onto the falling scenes. I uploaded the falling motion clip to Higgs Field and described the aesthetic I wanted for each one. Higgs Field is actually offering 33 days of unlimited scenes to 2.5 generations right now. So if you commented woe, I'll send you the link and my prompts as well. Now once you have your falling clips, add the Instagram top and bottom blocks to each one so that they look like posts in your feed. Now add all these videos to a new project and set the falling clips as overlays. Now to create the scroll effect, select your main clip and add a key frame at the moment that you fall into the hole. Then scroll forward and drag it up and off the screen. Now take your first falling video, add a key frame with the position below the frame, move forward and add a second key frame once it's fully on screen. Then move forward again and add a third key frame dragging it up and out of the frame. Repeat this for every falling clip so each one scrolls in as the last one scrolls out. And now you'll have something like...

classification.reason: Video reel with brief caption; queued for audio transcription

transcript: 3 edits and 30 seconds, let's go. First, we have the text behind effect. Import your video, duplicate it, and set the duplicate as an overlay. Click Remove Background and highlight the object you want in front. Then add your text and move the overlay to the top layer. And you're done. Next, the flash and edit. If you have CatCut Pro, just apply the Matte Snapshots effect. And if you don't, Instagram Edit has a similar effect called negative flash. Just add that and you're done. Okay, 10 seconds left. Finally, we have my signature shoe kick. To start, film yourself dropping your shoes and kicking them. Then film another video with your shoes on and kicking in the same direction. Cut the first clip when your feet touch the shoes and start the second one when your foot is in the same spot. And now you've learned.
